verdict.rationale: Bitwarden describes itself as an open source password manager, and community users say they chose it because its clients are not closed source; a commenter also thanks Bitwarden for relicensing back to a Free/Open license after the SDK controversy. The evidence is a vendor tagline plus community remarks, with no first-party docs on client repositories, licenses or review. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of client source repositories and their licenses, evidence that the TOTP/seed-handling code specifically is public, and independent audit or community-review evidence.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the client apps are open source, so the code handling my seeds can be inspected and community-reviewed

citations.quote: The most trusted open source password manager for passwords, passkeys, and secrets
I use BitWarden because I'd never trust a password manager with closed source clients
Thank you to Bitwarden for relicensing back to Free/Open License
